title: Хорёк
author: Лев Толстой
summary: A polecat licks a metalworker’s file and mistakes its own blood for iron. Complete fable.

source.editionId: First Russian Book for Reading, Хорёк; Wikisource revision 5737293

rights.original: Tolstoy (died 1910); underlying Russian work is public domain.
rights.transcription: Russian transcription from Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA; source page links to its revision history and terms.
rights.translation: New English translation for Slovarchik, CC BY-SA 4.0; no published translation reused.

translationReview.method: Checked both sentences against the pinned source, including the source’s unaccented «хорек» in the second sentence beside «Хорёк» in the first, which is kept as transcribed. The English keeps the fable’s single turn: the animal is pleased by what is destroying it.

sentences.ru: Хорёк зашел к меднику и стал лизать подпилок.
sentences.en: A polecat got into a coppersmith’s shop and began licking a file.

sentences.ru: Из языка пошла кровь, а хорек радовался, лизал, — думал, что из железа кровь идет, и погубил весь язык.
sentences.en: Blood ran from his tongue, and the polecat was delighted and went on licking — he thought the blood was coming out of the iron — and he ruined his whole tongue.
